chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that are great with Mankind, as they are running all the time, in that they [ ... ]
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by later Christian-connected comparison (Christ-name practices) and hagiographic self-presentation of Mani (“I, Manichaios…”, apostolate, rhetorical boasting, promise to believers). No systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping or impersonal cosmological mechanism appears; the chapter reads as editorial-apologetic material rather than the oldest teaching substrate.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening (“Once again he speaks”) marks hagiographic/dialogue frame; the content immediately anchors to “Christian people…”, indicating editorial setting rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Explicitly grounded in Christian practice and the name of “Christ”; this material enters via Christian tradition rather than the pre-compilation cosmological substrate.
Continues the list of Christian social practices surrounding devotion to Christ’s name (naming lovers/children). This is cosmos→community application, not internal cosmic system mapping.
Oath-taking “by his fortune and his surety… under his authority” remains within the Christian-social register; no cosmological correspondential structure is developed.

Autobiographical/hagiographic self-assertion (“I, Manichaios…”) with apostolic legitimation and claims of having ‘sown’ graces. This is community-edifying presentation of Mani, not the impersonal cosmological substrate.

Rhetorical boasting and exhortative invitation (“every one who will believe in me…”) belongs to apostolic self-presentation and community recruitment/edification; it is not a systematic cosmos→cosmos teaching layer.
